title: OWASP API1 — Broken Object Level Authorization
text: For each operation involving a caller-supplied object identifier, enforce an authorization decision for that specific object and authenticated identity. Authentication alone does not establish ownership. Restrict database queries to the trusted user's tenant or owner identifier; never trust owner identifiers supplied in the request.

title: CWE-639 — Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
text: A caller-controlled identifier can select another user's record when the application fails to bind that selection to the caller's permissions. Test with two users and verify that changing identifiers cannot cross an ownership boundary.

title: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention
text: Separate SQL structure from untrusted data using prepared statements and parameterized queries. Concatenating a request value into SQL can allow that value to change the statement's meaning. Review dynamic identifiers separately using allowlists.

title: OWASP OS Command Injection Defense
text: Prefer application libraries over operating system commands. When execution is unavoidable, use a fixed executable and separate argument arrays, avoid shell interpretation, and validate allowed inputs.

title: OWASP Secrets Management
text: Keep credentials outside application source. Use a secret manager or environment injection, limit privileges, and rotate exposed credentials. Deleting a secret from the current file does not invalidate copies in repository history.

title: OWASP API6 — Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
text: Identify sensitive business flows such as purchasing, reservation, credit, refund, transfer, and inventory operations. Define business and engineering protections for each flow; an endpoint is risky when it exposes a sensitive flow without appropriate restrictions.

title: OWASP Transaction Authorization
text: For sensitive transactions, authorize significant data server-side, control allowed state transitions, protect transaction data from modification, and ensure each transaction execution is properly authorized. Treat authorization and authentication as separate concerns.
